messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on rollout metadata — proposing a compact 'priority_hint' + 'tenant_override' surface. Short version: allow lightweight hints from multiple levels, resolve deterministically, and emit a small resolution trace for observability.

sam: Can you paste the sketch of the schema you're thinking of?

maria: Sure, rough draft below. Not final names, mostly to get consensus.

```json
{
  "priority_hint": {
    "level": "low|medium|high",        // human-friendly band
    "weight": 0,                           // numeric tie-breaker (higher wins)
    "origin": "client|route|tenant|global"
  },
  "tenant_override": {
    "mode": "allow|block|soft",       // allow = fully override, soft = hint only
    "expires_at": null                    // optional TTL for override
  },
  "stability_epoch": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ" // optional target epoch for canaries
}
```

alex: My main worry: enums + many small fields = schema sprawl. How do we keep this minimal for agents that only consume a couple of fields?

maria: Good call. Idea: core runtime only reads resolved fields: {effective_level, effective_weight, effective_origin}. All the hints are optional and used by control-plane resolution logic. Consumers can ignore the hint block.

jamie: For conflict resolution, I think a deterministic precedence should be documented. Proposal: precedence order = client > route > tenant-default > global. If origin ties, use weight; if still ties, break ties by lexicographic origin id (stable).

sam: +1. Also: what about backward compatibility with existing pin metadata? We have tenants that rely on 'anchor' semantics today.

maria: We map older fields during ingestion to the new hint model: legacy 'pin_strength' -> priority_hint.weight, legacy 'pin_source' -> origin. We'll keep a migration shim for 6mo and emit a warning event when legacy fields are used.

alex: Observability: we should capture a compact resolution_trace for each decision so ops can answer "why did tenant X get model Y". But keep trace small (1KB) and redact PII. Fields: [applied_sources, final_weight, rule_id, reason].

jamie: Also record metrics: gauge of effective_weight per tenant, counter of override_modes used (allow/soft/block), histogram of time-to-resolve for resolution logic.

maria: Agreed. Draft telemetry fields: resolution_trace (string, <= 1024 bytes), effective_level (enum), effective_weight (int), effective_origin (string), resolution_latency_ms (int). We'll add sampling for resolution_trace in high-volume routes.

sam: Edge-case: if tenant_override.mode=block, does that block all client hints? I assume yes. But what about 'soft' mode — client can suggest higher priority but tenant can veto if weight delta < threshold? Need deterministic rule.

maria: Proposal: block = absolute veto (ignore lower-level hints). soft = best-effort: allow client hints if client.weight - tenant.weight >= tenant.soft_threshold. Document soft_threshold default = 20.

alex: That threshold needs to be configurable at tenant level and emitted in telemetry. Also consider a safety cap so no single client can set extreme weight.

jamie: Implementation note for control-plane: resolution should be pure function of inputs so we can test. Also emit a canonical 'resolved_metadata' object to the route binder. That object contains only the minimal effective fields plus trace id.

maria: I'll draft a PR with schema + resolution algorithm + migration shim + telemetry tags. Plan to land as an RFC-followup patch and then a small canary.

sam: One more ask: add a small example to docs showing a tenant override that expires and a client reasserting priority afterwards. People find examples helpful.

maria: Will do.

deploy-bot: PR #1234 created: rollout-metadata/priority-hinting — includes schema, resolution tests, and metrics scaffolding.

ops-bot: Note: will schedule a 5% canary on dedicated pools after PR merge to validate behavioral parity.

maria: Thanks all — next steps: I'll open the RFC-followup PR description with the decision matrix and sample DSL examples. Ping me if you want to be reviewer. :thumbsup:
